items.title: Where rescue efforts stand at flood-hit hydropower projects
items.blurb: Two workers have been rescued, and bodies recovered, but teams are still searching flooded tunnels and damaged sites for hundreds of missing people.

items.title: Chinese national rescued alive after 10 days trapped in hydropower tunnel
items.blurb: Rescue teams also save a woman from a debris-buried house as search operations continue in flood-hit areas.

items.title: NEPSE falls as flood concerns weigh on insurance, hydropower
items.blurb: The index slips 0.57 percent in a four-session week, erasing about Rs30 billion in market value as thin trading and weak momentum keep the market near key support.

items.title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 1,342
items.blurb: Police say 4,886 people remain missing and 1,030 bodies have been buried as search operations continue.

items.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to address UN General Assembly on September 24
items.blurb: His first foreign trip since taking office comes as Nepal seeks international support after devastating floods.

items.title: 27 US lawmakers urge Rubio to expand rescue, aid efforts in Nepal
items.blurb: Lawmakers call for US disaster response team, high-altitude search assets and faster assistance as thousands remain missing.

items.title: Where to support flood relief in Kathmandu this week and beyond
items.blurb: From charity runs to creative workshops, these events offer ways to support flood-affected communities.

items.title: They stopped hoping to find him alive. Then they found a hand
items.blurb: Raj Kumar Diyali went missing with his wife and four-year-old son in Nepal’s Bhotekoshi flood. His family is now waiting for DNA confirmation.

items.title: Barely saved, he cuts mourning short to help flood survivors
items.blurb: Sudip Kumar Neupane watched a raging Trishuli swallow his younger brother and a close colleague, then came out of grief after two days.

items.title: Can Nepal turn Himalayan vulnerability into a case for compensation?
items.blurb: The Bhotekoshi disaster highlights rising climate risks in the Himalayas, but experts say Nepal needs stronger evidence, sharper diplomacy and a clear strategy to secure international grants.

items.title: After nine days in darkness, two men walked back into the light
items.blurb: Rescuers pulled Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan alive from the Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel after more than 72 hours of painstaking search, but dozens of people remain unaccounted for.

items.title: Why climate change is a threat to Nepal’s hydropower sector
items.blurb: Climate change is not a future risk to our hydropower sector; it is a present and recurring one. The August disaster proved it at a scale no prior monsoon had.

items.title: Five of 15 drinking water sources in flood-hit Bidur contaminated with E. coli
items.blurb: Officials mull cholera vaccination for around 100,000 vulnerable people and measles vaccine for over 75,000 children.

items.title: Nvidia donates $10 million to flood recovery, one of Nepal’s biggest corporate donations
items.blurb: The contribution, deposited into the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund, was driven by more than 50 Nepali employees of the US technology giant.

items.title: Road department begins cutting new track to reopen flood-hit Prithvi Highway
items.blurb: Authorities are widening a 50-metre temporary route around the Krishnabhir landslide on the highway.

items.title: Search and rescue team says ‘no more survivors in Upper Trishuli 3A tunnel’
items.blurb: After rescuing two survivors and finding a dead body, rescuers say they could not locate any more survivors or bodies.

items.title: Nepal home minister tells critics to focus on results, not where he works
items.blurb: Sudan Gurung defends coordinating the flood response online after social media criticism of his role in Friday’s tunnel rescue.

items.title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 1,287
items.blurb: Bodies have been recovered across eight districts, with Chitwan reporting the highest number of bodies at 359, followed by Nawalparasi East and Nawalparasi West.

items.title: Prime Minister Balendra Shah, Australia’s Anthony Albanese discuss flood response
items.blurb: Shah thanked Australia for its support in rescue and relief efforts and said Nepal was stepping up the search for Australians reported missing after the disaster.

items.title: How two Nepal hydropower workers survived nine days trapped underground
items.blurb: One stayed behind to help colleagues escape the flood; the other had travelled to the project for routine maintenance.
